questions.q: A shop owner in Owerri insured his stock against fire for a sum equal to its full value. A fire damaged stock worth ₦850,000. The damaged goods were later sold for ₦120,000 as salvage. How much should the insurer pay?
questions.explanation: Under the principle of indemnity, the insured is restored to the financial position before the loss, but the salvage value reduces the actual loss. The payable amount is ₦850,000 − ₦120,000 = ₦730,000. Paying ₦850,000 would overcompensate, because the owner already recovered ₦120,000 from the salvage sale.

questions.q: A business owner in Lagos takes out a policy that will compensate her if a cashier dishonestly takes money from the till. The policy is known as
questions.explanation: Fidelity guarantee insurance covers the employer against loss caused by the dishonesty or fraud of employees entrusted with money or property. Money insurance covers loss of money in transit or on business premises, while burglary insurance covers theft following forced entry.

questions.q: A wholesaler supplies a retailer with goods on the understanding that the retailer may return any unsold goods within an agreed period. This practice is called
questions.explanation: In a sale-or-return arrangement, the retailer takes goods for resale but can return unsold items within the agreed period. Hire purchase involves payment by instalments and eventual ownership after the final payment, while a credit sale makes the buyer immediately liable to pay.

questions.q: A retail outlet is owned by its members, who buy goods from it regularly and share any surplus in proportion to their purchases. This type of retailer is a
questions.explanation: A consumer co-operative is owned and controlled by its consumer members, and any surplus is usually shared according to members' purchases. A departmental store and a multiple shop are owned by a business, not by their customers.

questions.q: A wholesale trader in Ondo sorts bags of cocoa into first, second and third qualities before selling them to exporters. This function is called
questions.explanation: Grading is the process of sorting goods into classes or qualities according to size, quality or other standards before sale. Breaking bulk means dividing large quantities into smaller units, while storage means keeping goods until they are needed.

questions.q: The voting rights attached to ordinary shares enable the holders mainly to
options: receive a fixed rate of interest every year
demand automatic repayment of their capital after five years
be paid before preference shareholders when dividends are declared
participate in electing directors and deciding major company matters
questions.explanation: Ordinary shareholders usually exercise voting rights at general meetings, especially to elect directors and approve major decisions. They do not receive fixed interest, are paid dividends after preference shareholders, and cannot demand automatic repayment of their capital.

questions.q: Which of the following is a technological obstacle to e-commerce in many rural areas of Nigeria?
options: the display of product prices on websites
the availability of goods for sale online
the desire of buyers to compare prices
poor internet connectivity and unstable electricity
questions.explanation: E-commerce depends on electricity and internet connectivity, which are unreliable in many rural areas. Online stores can display prices, and buyers generally need to compare prices, so those are not valid obstacles.

questions.q: Sales of a particular brand of soap in Kano have fallen steadily for two years, and many retailers now order it only occasionally. The brand is most likely in which stage of its product life cycle?
questions.explanation: A product in decline experiences falling sales and reduced interest from retailers. Introduction has low but rising sales, growth has rapidly increasing sales, while maturity usually has stable or only slowly changing sales.

questions.q: A beverage company in Ibadan sponsors the construction of a community borehole and publishes the story in newspapers. This activity is best described as
questions.explanation: Public relations is concerned with building goodwill and favourable relationships with the public through activities such as sponsorship and publicity. Sales promotion offers short-term purchase incentives, while personal selling involves direct contact with a buyer.

questions.q: An exporter in Aba wants to give a foreign buyer details of the price, quantity, quality and terms of a proposed supply before a firm order is placed. He should send a
questions.explanation: A proforma invoice is a preliminary quotation or invoice sent before a sale is concluded. A commercial invoice is issued after the goods are sold, a bill of exchange orders payment, and a delivery note accompanies goods being delivered.

questions.q: A document drawn by one person on another requiring the latter to pay a stated sum of money to a named person on demand or at a future date is called a
questions.explanation: A bill of exchange is an unconditional written order by one party to another to pay a specified sum to a named person. A promissory note is only a promise to pay, while a letter of credit is a bank's undertaking to make payment when specified conditions are met.

questions.q: When a Nigerian trader buys motorcycles from India, the transaction is recorded in the balance of payments as
options: A credit in the current account
A debit in the capital account
A debit in the current account
A credit in the capital account
questions.explanation: Imports of goods are recorded as a debit in the visible trade section of the current account because payment flows out of the country. The capital account deals mainly with financial assets and liabilities, not ordinary goods imports.

questions.q: A Nigerian importer in Kaduna wants foreign exchange to pay for goods from Japan. The document he completes to validate the import transaction with an authorised dealer bank is
questions.explanation: Form M is an import declaration form used in Nigeria to validate eligible imports and support the purchase of foreign exchange through an authorised dealer bank. A bill of lading is a carrier's receipt for goods, while a bill of exchange is an instruction to pay.

questions.q: The consumer right that protects a buyer from goods that can cause injury or harm is the right to
questions.explanation: The right to safety protects consumers against goods that are hazardous to health or life. The right to redress concerns compensation for wrongs suffered, while the right to be heard concerns expressing complaints.

questions.q: Ani, a cloth seller in Aba, wants to send a sample of lace to a customer in Kaduna with a guarantee that the parcel will be delivered and signed for. Which service should Ani use?
questions.explanation: A courier service is suitable because it handles parcels and gives a record of delivery, often with the recipient's signature. Ordinary letter post is not intended for parcels, while money order and business reply service serve different payment or response purposes.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major advantage of written communication over oral communication in a business office?
options: It is best for settling an urgent dispute on the spot.
It provides a permanent record of the message.
questions.explanation: Written communication can be filed and referred to later, so it provides a permanent record. Immediate feedback, personal contact and on-the-spot settlement of disputes are advantages more associated with oral communication.

questions.q: A trader in Enugu needs cash before the due date of a bill of exchange. He hands the bill to a bank, which pays him less than the face value. The amount deducted by the bank is known as
questions.explanation: When a bank discounts a bill before maturity, it deducts an amount known as discount from the face value. Commission is a fee for an agent's service, premium is commonly an insurance payment, and service charge is a general bank charge.

questions.q: A trader moves yams from a village in Benue to a market in Lagos where they are needed. The utility created by this movement is
questions.explanation: Moving goods from where they are less needed to where they are needed creates place utility. Form utility comes from changing the form of a product, time utility from making it available at the right time, and possession utility from transferring ownership.

questions.q: Chika combines her savings, a shop and the services of two assistants to start a provisions business, and she bears any loss the business makes. Chika is performing the function of an
questions.explanation: An entrepreneur organises land, labour and capital and bears the risk of the business. A landlord supplies land or premises for rent, a creditor lends money, and a consumer uses goods and services.

questions.q: Amina, a teacher in Sokoto, takes a life policy that pays a stated sum to her family only if she dies within the next 20 years. If she survives the period, the insurer pays nothing. This policy is an example of
questions.explanation: A term insurance policy provides cover for a fixed period and pays only if death occurs within that period. Whole life assurance covers the insured for life, while an endowment policy pays on survival at the end of the term as well as on death within it.

questions.q: A trader in Ogbomoso insures her stock for ₦1,500,000 at a rate of 2½% per annum. What annual premium does she pay?
questions.explanation: Annual premium = 2.5% × ₦1,500,000 = ₦37,500. Using 0.25% instead of 2.5% would wrongly give ₦3,750.

questions.q: Musa, a retailer in Ilorin, receives a consignment of shoes from a wholesaler on the understanding that he will pay for only those he sells and return the rest. This arrangement is known as
questions.explanation: Under sale or return, the retailer takes goods to sell but may return unsold items to the wholesaler. Hire purchase involves paying by instalments before ownership passes, while trade credit is a period allowed before payment.

questions.q: Olamide buys a television on hire purchase from a retailer in Lagos. Until the final instalment is paid, ownership of the television remains with
questions.explanation: In hire purchase, the buyer receives the goods and pays by instalments, but ownership passes only after the final payment. The seller keeps ownership until then, even though the buyer is using the television.

questions.q: An investor bought 1,000 ordinary shares of a company at ₦12.00 per share. The company declared a dividend of 90 kobo per share. What is the dividend yield on the investor's cost?
questions.explanation: Dividend yield = dividend per share ÷ cost per share × 100 = ₦0.90 ÷ ₦12.00 × 100 = 7.5%. The total dividend of ₦900 divided by the total cost of ₦12,000 also gives 7.5%.

questions.q: A client instructs his stockbroker to sell 500 shares of a company, but not at a price below ₦20.00 per share. This instruction is a
questions.explanation: A limit order states the minimum price at which the investor is willing to sell, and the shares will not be sold below that price. A market order would be executed immediately at the best price currently available.

questions.q: A pharmacy in Ikeja sells medicines to individual patients through its website and delivers the medicines to their homes. This is an example of
questions.explanation: The pharmacy is a business selling directly to individual final consumers, which is business-to-consumer e-commerce. Business-to-business e-commerce would involve transactions between one business and another.

questions.q: An online shop in Lagos hopes to sell to customers in a rural community in Taraba, but many residents there have no internet access or smartphones. The main effect of this situation on the shop is that
options: its prices must be fixed by the government
its website will attract more buyers
its goods cannot be transported to Taraba
questions.explanation: E-commerce depends on customers having access to the internet and devices for online transactions. Without such access, many residents cannot buy from the online shop, so the shop's potential market is smaller. Transport problems would affect delivery after an online sale, not the ability to reach customers online.

questions.q: During a Christmas promotion, a bakery in Enugu gives one free loaf to any customer who buys three loaves. This is best described as...
questions.explanation: A short-term incentive such as a free loaf is a sales promotion designed to encourage immediate buying. Personal selling uses direct contact with a salesperson, while advertising is paid communication through media.

questions.q: A newly established microfinance bank in Awka places a newspaper advertisement listing its savings account types, minimum deposit and branch addresses. The advertisement is mainly...
questions.explanation: Informative advertising gives facts that help prospective customers understand a new product or service. Persuasive advertising tries to win preference, while reminder advertising keeps an established brand in the buyer's mind.

questions.q: A hotel in Port Harcourt asks a furniture maker in Aba to state the price, delivery period and payment terms for 20 beds before it decides whether to place an order. The document the furniture maker should send is a...
questions.explanation: A pro forma invoice sets out proposed prices and terms before a sale is completed. A credit note corrects an overcharge, a statement of account shows a balance, and a bill of lading is a transport document.

questions.q: A manufacturer discovers that a batch of electric kettles it sold in Ibadan can overheat and cause fire. The manufacturer asks retailers to withdraw the kettles from sale and advises buyers to return them for repair. This action is called...
questions.explanation: A product recall withdraws defective goods from the market to prevent harm to consumers. A warranty claim is a buyer's request for repair or replacement, and a trade description identifies or describes goods.

questions.q: A trader in Owerri sells a pressing iron to a customer, but the iron stops working after two days. The seller refuses to repair, replace or refund the money. The customer's right to obtain a remedy for this loss is known as the right to...
questions.explanation: The right to redress entitles a consumer to compensation, repair, replacement or refund when goods are defective. The right to choose concerns selection among alternatives, and the right to safety concerns protection from harm.

questions.q: A haulage company in Jos covers goods on open trucks with tarpaulins mainly to protect them from
questions.explanation: Tarpaulins are waterproof covers used mainly to shield goods from rain, dust and similar weather conditions during road transport. They do not remove customs duty or significantly reduce fuel consumption.

questions.q: A farmer near Makurdi wants to move fresh tomatoes to Enugu quickly to reduce spoilage. The farm is not served by rail or airport. The most suitable mode of transport is
questions.explanation: Road transport is the most suitable because it can provide flexible door-to-door movement and does not depend on rail or airport facilities. It can also be organised quickly for perishable goods such as fresh tomatoes.

questions.q: The management of a school in Ibadan puts a notice on the staff notice board announcing a change in resumption time. This is an example of
questions.explanation: The message flows from management to staff, so it is downward communication. Upward communication would flow from subordinates to superiors, while horizontal communication is between people of similar rank.

questions.q: An instrument prepared by a bank in favour of a named payee after the amount has been paid to the bank in advance is called a
questions.explanation: A bank draft is prepared by a bank and the amount is paid in advance, making it a secure means of payment to a named payee. A personal cheque is drawn by an individual, while a bill of exchange is a general negotiable instrument.

questions.q: A group of cocoa farmers in Ondo State forms an organisation to buy inputs, process their cocoa and sell the product on their behalf. The organisation is best described as a
questions.explanation: A producers' cooperative society is owned and controlled by producers who pool resources for buying inputs, processing and marketing their products. A trade union mainly protects the interests of workers, not the processing and marketing of members' produce.

questions.q: The document issued by the Corporate Affairs Commission as evidence that a private limited company has been legally registered is the
questions.explanation: The certificate of incorporation is issued after a company has satisfied registration requirements and is evidence that the company legally exists. The memorandum and articles of association are documents submitted during registration, while a prospectus invites the public to subscribe for shares.

questions.q: A dough-mixing machine used in a bakery in Ibadan is classified under which factor of production?
questions.explanation: A dough-mixing machine is a man-made resource used to produce goods and is therefore capital. Land refers to natural resources, labour is human effort, and entrepreneurship coordinates the other factors and bears risk.

questions.q: A trader in Abeokuta insured his warehouse and stock for ₦2,000,000, which was their full value. Fire damaged goods valued at ₦600,000. How much will the insurer pay as indemnity?
options: ₦1,400,000, being the balance of the sum insured
₦600,000, being the actual amount of the loss suffered
Nothing, because the whole warehouse was not destroyed
questions.explanation: The principle of indemnity restores the insured to the financial position before the loss, so payment is based on the actual loss suffered. Since the sum insured is equal to the full value and is sufficient to cover the loss, the insurer pays ₦600,000, not the full sum insured.

questions.q: A shop owner in Ibadan insured stock worth ₦800,000 for ₦600,000 against fire. A fire destroyed stock valued at ₦200,000. If the policy contains an average clause, how much will the insurer pay?
questions.explanation: Under the average clause, the claim is reduced in proportion to the underinsurance: (₦600,000 ÷ ₦800,000) × ₦200,000 = ₦150,000. Paying ₦200,000 would ignore the average clause and overcompensate the insured.

questions.q: A retailer in Kaduna returned damaged goods to a wholesaler and later received a document reducing the amount owed on the account. The document received is a
questions.explanation: A credit note is sent by a seller to reduce the buyer's indebtedness when goods are returned or an overcharge is corrected. A debit note increases the amount owed, while a delivery note merely accompanies goods and does not adjust the account.

questions.q: A wholesaler in Aba is able to sell goods to retailers at lower prices than consumers normally pay mainly because the wholesaler
options: buys in large quantities and enjoys trade discounts from manufacturers
stores goods in many small kiosks
sells goods on credit to final consumers
questions.explanation: Wholesalers buy in bulk and often receive trade discounts, enabling them to sell to retailers at lower prices. Selling on credit, advertising, or using small kiosks does not by itself explain the lower wholesale prices.

questions.q: Which of the following transactions is an example of business-to-business e-commerce?
options: A retiree in Ibadan pays her electricity bill through a bank app
A bakery in Lagos buys flour online from a flour mill
A family in Abuja orders groceries through a supermarket website
A student in Enugu buys a textbook from an online bookshop
questions.explanation: Business-to-business e-commerce involves transactions between two businesses. A bakery buying flour online from a flour mill is a business dealing with another business, while the other transactions involve final consumers.

questions.q: A beverage distributor in Enugu divides the city's buyers into groups such as students, office workers and low-income earners before deciding how to advertise to each group. This practice is known as
questions.explanation: Market segmentation is the division of a market into groups of buyers with similar needs or characteristics so that each group can be served or advertised to more effectively. Market penetration is about increasing sales in an existing market, while product differentiation is about making a product appear different from competing brands.

questions.q: A small furniture maker in Ibadan combines the design of his chairs, the price he charges, the showroom where he sells them and the advertisement he places in a local newspaper. In marketing, this combination is called the
questions.explanation: The marketing mix is the combination of product, price, place and promotion used to satisfy customers and achieve marketing goals. Marketing research is the gathering of information, the product life cycle describes stages in a product's market life, and channels of distribution concern only how goods reach users.

questions.q: A trader in Jos receives cartons of soap from a supplier in Kano. The document he signs to show that the goods listed have been received is a
questions.explanation: A delivery note accompanies goods and is signed by the receiver to acknowledge that the listed goods have been delivered. A pro-forma invoice gives stated selling terms before a firm sale, a debit note requests additional payment after undercharging, and a certificate of origin shows the country where goods were produced.

questions.q: A consumer in Port Harcourt buys a generator from a dealer, but it develops a fault. The consumer wants to complain to the dealer and seek redress. Keeping the sales receipt is most important because it
options: provides proof of the purchase and its details
forces the dealer to replace every faulty product
prevents the product from developing further faults
questions.explanation: A sales receipt is evidence that a purchase was made and usually shows the date, item, price and seller, which helps a consumer make a complaint and seek redress. It does not by itself extend a warranty, compel replacement in every case, or stop a product from developing faults.

questions.q: A hairdresser in Akure plaits a customer's hair and is paid immediately after the service. This occupation is best classified as
questions.explanation: Direct personal services are rendered directly to a person and are consumed as they are provided, as when a hairdresser plaits hair for a fee. Indirect commercial services such as banking and transport facilitate trade; they do not produce raw materials or manufacture goods.

questions.q: A group of market women in Onitsha wants to pool their savings and lend to one another at moderate interest. The type of cooperative society most suitable for them is a
questions.explanation: A credit and thrift cooperative society collects members' savings and lends to members at moderate interest. Consumer cooperatives sell goods to members, marketing cooperatives help sell members' produce, and producer cooperatives support production activities.

questions.q: While listening to a radio advertisement, a customer's phone signal keeps breaking up, so she cannot clearly hear the advertised price. In the communication process, the break-up is an example of
questions.explanation: Noise is any interference that distorts or blocks a message as it moves from sender to receiver, such as a poor phone signal. Feedback is the receiver's response, encoding is converting an idea into words or symbols, and the medium is the channel used to carry the message.

questions.q: A cheque dated 10 January is presented for payment at a bank on 20 July of the same year. The cheque will most likely be rejected because it is
questions.explanation: A cheque is normally valid for six months, so a cheque dated 10 January becomes stale after 10 July of the same year. A crossed cheque can still be paid through a bank, a post-dated cheque bears a future date, and a bearer cheque is payable to the person presenting it.

questions.q: Tunde operates a supermarket in Ikeja, while Bisi runs a small provision store nearby. Which of the following is an advantage Tunde's business has over Bisi's store?
options: He can buy in larger quantities and obtain trade discounts.
He can grant longer credit to every customer without keeping records.
He can operate with lower total overhead costs than the small store.
He can give personal attention to each individual customer more easily.
questions.explanation: Buying in large quantities enables a supermarket to obtain trade discounts and sell at competitive prices. Personal attention and low total overhead are usually strengths of a small provision store, not a large supermarket.

questions.q: A wholesaler in Port Harcourt buys oranges in large quantities from farmers and keeps them in cold storage until retailers need them. Which function of the wholesaler does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Keeping goods in cold storage until they are needed is the storage function. Transportation involves moving goods, grading involves sorting by quality, and risk bearing concerns losses that may occur.

questions.q: A young entrepreneur in Makurdi sells handmade bags through an online store. Which of the following is the greatest advantage this gives her over selling only from a local shop?
options: Every buyer can physically examine the bags before paying.
She can reach customers in places far beyond Makurdi.
Her goods automatically become cheaper than all locally made bags.
She no longer needs to arrange for delivery of goods.
questions.explanation: E-commerce lets a seller overcome distance and reach a wider market. It does not remove delivery needs, allow physical examination before purchase, or guarantee lower prices.

questions.q: A customer in Enugu orders a pair of shoes from an online store. When the shoes arrive, they are the right colour but the wrong size. Which challenge of e-commerce does this illustrate?
options: The goods cannot be delivered outside the seller's town.
The seller has no way of advertising goods to customers.
The buyer cannot use electronic payment for online purchases.
The buyer cannot physically inspect the goods before purchase.
questions.explanation: In online shopping, the customer usually chooses from pictures and descriptions and may not try on or examine the item before paying. Electronic payment, advertising and delivery are not the issue in this case.

questions.q: A small fashion designer in Abuja wants to display photographs of new designs to many young customers at relatively low cost. Which advertising medium is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Social media allows photographs of designs to be shown to a large, young audience at relatively low cost and with targeting. Radio cannot show the designs, while newspapers and billboards are usually more costly for a small designer seeking many young customers.

questions.q: A manufacturer in Kano prints a special smiling-farmer emblem on every bag of rice so buyers can recognise it among similar bags. What is this practice called?
questions.explanation: Branding gives a product a distinctive name, symbol or design so that buyers can identify and distinguish it from competing products. Packaging mainly contains and protects the product, while labelling mainly provides information about it.

questions.q: A supermarket in Lagos places sweets and chewing gum on racks near the pay point so customers can pick them while waiting to pay. This arrangement is intended mainly to encourage
questions.explanation: Goods placed near the pay point are meant to prompt customers to buy them without prior planning, which is impulse buying. Bulk buying involves large quantities, hire purchase involves payment by instalments, and window shopping is inspecting goods without buying.

questions.q: A customer in Ibadan wants to buy 20 cartons of detergent from a manufacturer and sends a document stating the quantity, delivery date and price he is willing to pay. Which document has the customer issued?
questions.explanation: A purchase order is the buyer’s formal request to a supplier to supply stated goods on specified terms. A proforma invoice is sent by the seller as a quotation, while an advice note and a consignment note are used around dispatch and carriage of goods.
